## Classification and limits

Version-set equality proves ledger parity only, not schema equivalence or execution success. Local-only versions require schema/object inspection before applying or repairing; remote-only versions require recovering original reviewed SQL. Never replay the full historical set with db push --include-all. RLS counts do not prove policy correctness, grants, view security, or absence of public data exposure.

Existing docs conflict: scripts/check-migration-drift.mjs says ledger reconciled in July; docs/ops-runbook.md still warns of >100 missing historical entries. Use this dated observation for current version-set status; preserve incident history separately.

## Safe next steps

1. Re-run duplicate guard and ledger-set comparison in strict CI; investigate any mismatch before release.
2. For full DB-1 closure, compare a clean migration replay schema with production catalog objects, grants, policies, indexes and function definitions using normalized hashes. Ledger parity alone is insufficient.
3. Exercise pgTAP concurrency/security tests on staging; audit role-effective policies before any production change.
